searchBreadth: Six distinct opportunities across everyday mathematics/design, tactile language, astronomy, information systems, cultural-material history and ecology. Search opened institutional bodies where available; failed access stays explicit. The pool is a bounded sample of an open universe, not a whitelist.

candidates.subject: The rectangle that survives halving
candidates.novelty: A familiar object becomes a miniature proof, distinct from prior material, time-navigation and traffic mechanisms.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: ISO/DIN/Cambridge provide central evidence plus independent algebra.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: Understand why this ratio preserves shape and why half the area is not half the length.
candidates.visualPotential: Cut, rotate and overlay the same geometry; use an original print layout to demonstrate scaling.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: A4 appears mundane until a square fails the same test.
candidates.productionFeasibility: New bespoke paper choreography is feasible locally; exact geometry matters more than realism.
candidates.portfolioDiversity: Adds everyday mathematical design without imposing a new domain preference.
candidates.comparison: Stronger immediate visual proof and fewer empirical caveats than the other current candidates.
limitations: No performance forecast or owner topic approval claimed.

candidates.subject: Why braille uses six dots
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: LOC body inspected; detailed chronology needs further bounded research.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: Distinguish tactile literacy design from visually imitating printed letters.
candidates.visualPotential: Macro raised dots and a well-qualified tactile demonstration.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: A small design decision opens a whole writing system.
candidates.productionFeasibility: Original modeling feasible; a faceless depiction must not invent user experience.
candidates.comparison: Strong future candidate, but the paper story resolves its central mechanism more directly within a short.
limitations: No performance forecast or owner topic approval claimed.

candidates.subject: The Moon is moving away
candidates.novelty: New mechanism; overlaps prior space-scale portfolio.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: NASA body inspected; tidal mechanism can be corroborated with primary literature.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: Explain how ranging reveals orbital evolution.
candidates.visualPotential: Laser-return and energy-transfer views, not a simple scale montage.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: The Moon changes distance while it looks constant.
candidates.productionFeasibility: New orbital mechanism feasible; preserve present-rate scope.
candidates.portfolioDiversity: Astronomy is eligible without receiving automatic preference.
candidates.comparison: Strong curiosity, but central-rate extrapolation risk and portfolio overlap reduce its advantage today.
limitations: No performance forecast or owner topic approval claimed.

candidates.subject: A barcode digit checks the others
candidates.novelty: Everyday systems explanation distinct from history.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: GS1 result found; body open failed and algorithm not yet inspected.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: Explain error detection without promising authentication.
candidates.visualPotential: Digits, weighted sums and a deliberate typo.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: The last digit has a hidden job.
candidates.productionFeasibility: Original arithmetic visuals feasible after central evidence acquisition.
candidates.comparison: Hold because central-source body access is incomplete, not because its domain is excluded.
limitations: Discovery lead only; not claim verification.

candidates.subject: Purple made from sea snails
candidates.novelty: Cultural-material story, distinct from chocolate phase structure.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: Smithsonian result located; body open failed.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: Explain a material source behind historical color prestige.
candidates.visualPotential: Original mollusk and dye-process reconstruction with historical scope.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: A luxurious color begins with an unexpected animal.
candidates.productionFeasibility: New illustration feasible, but period costume and extraction details need rights and evidence care.
candidates.comparison: No central source body yet; avoid repeating sensational snail counts or universal royalty restrictions.
limitations: Discovery lead only; not claim verification.

candidates.subject: Many trunks, one clonal system
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: NPS body inspected; quantitative Pando age/extent not yet substantiated.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: Distinguish individual stems from connected clone identity.
candidates.visualPotential: Forest-to-root reveal with a truthful scale disclosure.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: What looks like many trees can share one root system.
candidates.productionFeasibility: Original ecological imagery possible; connection/identity caveats require additional scrutiny.
candidates.portfolioDiversity: Eligible nature, without inheriting Wood Frog style.
candidates.comparison: Excellent future candidate; paper offers a clearer bounded proof with fewer biological ambiguities.
limitations: No performance forecast or owner topic approval claimed.

rationale: Select A-series paper for an immediately visible paradox, rigorous but accessible proof, useful scaling payoff, source feasibility and portfolio novelty. New paper-specific scenes will serve the mechanism; no old renderer/style or storage preference influenced selection.
